precepts.text: The everlasting covenant of the priesthood with Aaron and his seed: to offer the sacrifices and to teach Jacob the testimonies and inform Israel in His laws.
precepts.point: That is why leadership today is not walking around requiring Levite lineage of Aaron. Christ is the high priest now, and the nation is a whole nation of kings and priests; Malachi and Hebrews are two good books to study on the changing of the priesthood, against the doctrine that the Aaronic covenant could never change.

note.label: Exodus 29: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

precepts.why:
Ecclesiasticus records the same consecration: “Moses consecrated him, and anointed him with holy oil: this was appointed unto him by an everlasting covenant, and to his seed, so long as the heavens should remain, that they should minister unto him, and execute the office of the priesthood, and bless the people in his name.” That is the perpetual statute of the priest's office to Aaron and his sons.

The Most High “chose him out of all men living to offer sacrifices to the Lord, incense, and a sweet savour, for a memorial, to make reconciliation for his people.” And He gave him “his commandments, and authority in the statutes of judgments, that he should teach Jacob the testimonies, and inform Israel in his laws.”

So the priest's job was two things: the offerings, and teaching the nation the law, statutes and commandments.

precepts.text: And now, O ye priests, this commandment is for you; the chapter is spoken to the priests.
precepts.point: That is why leadership today is not walking around requiring Levite lineage of Aaron. Christ is the high priest now, and the nation is a whole nation of kings and priests; Malachi and Hebrews are two good books to study on the changing of the priesthood, against the doctrine that the Aaronic covenant could never change.

note.label: Exodus 29: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

precepts.why:
“And now, O ye priests, this commandment is for you.” The whole chapter is spoken to the priests, the seed of Aaron who were consecrated in Exodus 29 for a perpetual statute.

What happened to that everlasting covenant of the priesthood is answered here, in a commandment aimed straight at the priests themselves.

precepts.text: The covenant with Levi was of life and peace and the priest is the messenger of the Lord of hosts; but ye are departed out of the way, caused many to stumble at the law, and have corrupted the covenant of Levi.
precepts.point: That is why leadership today is not walking around requiring Levite lineage of Aaron. Christ is the high priest now, and the nation is a whole nation of kings and priests; Malachi and Hebrews are two good books to study on the changing of the priesthood, against the doctrine that the Aaronic covenant could never change.

note.label: Exodus 29: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

precepts.why:
“My covenant was with him of life and peace”: the covenant with Levi. “The law of truth was in his mouth, and iniquity was not found in his lips: he walked with me in peace and equity, and did turn many away from iniquity.” That was the priest's office as it was given: “For the priest’s lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth: for he is the messenger of the Lord of hosts.”

“But ye are departed out of the way; ye have caused many to stumble at the law; ye have corrupted the covenant of Levi, saith the Lord of hosts.” The priests were finessing the offerings, keeping the best animals for themselves and sacrificing the blind and the broken, and they perverted the teachings of the law for their own benefit. Both parts of the job Ecclesiasticus lays out, the sacrifices and the teaching, they corrupted.

That is why leadership today is not walking around requiring Levite lineage of Aaron. Christ is the high priest now, and the nation is a whole nation of kings and priests. Malachi and Hebrews are two good books to study on the changing of the priesthood, against the doctrine that the Aaronic covenant could never change.

precepts.text: Be no more children tossed to and fro and carried about with every wind of doctrine, by the sleight of men.
precepts.point: These ordinances belonged to the Levitical priesthood, and the doctrines that would put men back under pieces of that office today do not even keep what they claim; they sound right because they use scriptures strongly and confidently, but they are in error. Be not tossed to and fro with every wind of doctrine, nor carried about with strange doctrines; do not ever fall away from the Messiah.

note.label: Exodus 29: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

precepts.why:
The ram of consecration, the blood on the right ear, the thumb and the great toe, the wave offering and the heave offering that Aaron and his sons received “by a statute for ever from the children of Israel”: these ordinances belonged to the Levitical priesthood. You will read about the wave offering and the heave offering throughout the first five books, Leviticus predominantly.

The doctrines that would put men back under pieces of that office today do not even keep what they claim. They sound right because they use scriptures strongly and confidently, but they are in error. “That we henceforth be no more children, tossed to and fro, and carried about with every wind of doctrine, by the sleight of men, and cunning craftiness, whereby they lie in wait to deceive”. Sleight of men and cunning craftiness is exactly how those doctrines are carried.

precepts.text: Be not carried about with divers and strange doctrines; the heart is established with grace, not with meats.
precepts.point: These ordinances belonged to the Levitical priesthood, and the doctrines that would put men back under pieces of that office today do not even keep what they claim; they sound right because they use scriptures strongly and confidently, but they are in error. Be not tossed to and fro with every wind of doctrine, nor carried about with strange doctrines; do not ever fall away from the Messiah.

note.label: Exodus 29: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

precepts.why:
“Be not carried about with divers and strange doctrines. For it is a good thing that the heart be established with grace; not with meats, which have not profited them that have been occupied therein.”

The consecration ram, the wave offering and the heave offering were meats of the Levitical priesthood. The heart is established with grace, not with those meats. Doctrines that would put men back under pieces of that office use the scriptures strongly and confidently, yet do not keep what they claim; do not be carried about with them, and do not ever fall away from the Messiah.

precepts.text: I am in the midst of Israel, and I am the Lord your God, and none else; everyone else is excluded, and my people shall never be ashamed.
precepts.point: He brought them forth out of the land of Egypt that He may dwell among them: I am the Lord their God. Israel should walk confident, special, and chosen above all nations of people, for the Most High is faithful and belongs to no one else; repent from spiritual fornication and return to the Most High.

note.label: Exodus 29: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

precepts.why:
“I will dwell among the children of Israel, and will be their God.” Joel says the same: “And ye shall know that I am in the midst of Israel, and that I am the Lord your God, and none else: and my people shall never be ashamed.”

He was in no other nation's tabernacle, temple or synagogue. There is no tabernacle today, but it is still the same case: He is in the midst of Israel and none else, which excludes everybody else from the benefits of having the Most High as their God.

There is nothing to be ashamed of in the fact that He chose Israel only; “my people shall never be ashamed.” Israel should walk confident, special and chosen above all nations of people, for the Most High is faithful and belongs to no one else.

precepts.text: Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, for he hath visited and redeemed his people; the God of the Bible is the God of Israel in both testaments.
precepts.point: He brought them forth out of the land of Egypt that He may dwell among them: I am the Lord their God. Israel should walk confident, special, and chosen above all nations of people, for the Most High is faithful and belongs to no one else; repent from spiritual fornication and return to the Most High.

note.label: Exodus 29: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

precepts.why:
Nothing changed across testaments. In Exodus the Lord says, “I will dwell among the children of Israel, and will be their God”, and in the gospel: “Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; for he hath visited and redeemed his people”.

The God of the Bible is the God of Israel in both testaments, and that is the purpose of Christ: to redeem His people. He that brought them forth out of the land of Egypt that He may dwell among them is the same Lord God of Israel who visited and redeemed them.

precepts.text: The adversaries said, Let us build with you, for we seek your God; the fathers answered, Ye have nothing to do with us, but we ourselves together will build unto the Lord God of Israel.
precepts.point: He brought them forth out of the land of Egypt that He may dwell among them: I am the Lord their God. Israel should walk confident, special, and chosen above all nations of people, for the Most High is faithful and belongs to no one else; repent from spiritual fornication and return to the Most High.

note.label: Exodus 29: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

precepts.why:
The other nations knew whose God He was. “Now when the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin heard that the children of the captivity builded the temple unto the Lord God of Israel”, they came to Zerubbabel and the chief of the fathers and said, “Let us build with you: for we seek your God, as ye do”.

The answer: “Ye have nothing to do with us to build an house unto our God; but we ourselves together will build unto the Lord God of Israel”. Zerubbabel, Jeshua and the chief of the fathers knew that the Lord dwells among the children of Israel and is their God, and no one else's.

That is the mindset for these last days. Israel does not need the other nations' assistance; the nation rebuilds one another spiritually, ourselves together, while awaiting Christ's return to restore the kingdom. Repent from spiritual fornication and return to the Most High, who belongs to no one else.

precepts.text: Sanctify the breast of the wave offering, and the shoulder of the heave offering, which is waved, and which is heaved up; the offering was lifted and waved before the Lord.
precepts.point: The wave breast and the heave shoulder were given to Aaron the priest and his sons by a statute for ever; this is how the priests ate from the peace offerings. Leviticus 10 returns to these portions, the wave breast and heave shoulder given to Aaron and his sons and daughters; chapters 6 through 10 explain the offerings.

note.label: Leviticus 7: Christ Our Peace Offering

precepts.why:
Moses was told, “thou shalt sanctify the breast of the wave offering, and the shoulder of the heave offering, which is waved, and which is heaved up, of the ram of the consecration, even of that which is for Aaron, and of that which is for his sons”.

Which is waved, and which is heaved up: the offering was lifted and waved before the Lord as a sign, proof of what the man had brought with his own hands. The wave breast and the heave shoulder then belonged to Aaron and his sons by a statute for ever; this is how the priests ate from the peace offerings, and Leviticus 10 returns to these same portions.

precepts.text: The wave offering was waved in the hands of Aaron and his sons before the Lord and then burnt on the altar, and the wave breast and heave shoulder were the priests' part from the children of Israel for ever.
precepts.point: It is a covenant of salt for ever before the Lord, unto Aaron and to his seed with him, the children that come after them.

note.label: Numbers 18: The Charge and Portion of the Priests and Levites

precepts.why:
The flesh of the firstlings was the priest's, “as the wave breast and as the right shoulder are thine”, and all the heave offerings of the holy things were given to Aaron and his sons and daughters by a statute for ever, to the lineage of the Levites. Exodus 29 shows how the wave offering and the heave offering were done.

“And thou shalt put all in the hands of Aaron, and in the hands of his sons; and shalt wave them for a wave offering before the Lord. And thou shalt receive them of their hands, and burn them upon the altar for a burnt offering, for a sweet savour before the Lord.” The wave offering was put in the hands of Aaron and his sons and waved, meaning shaken, before the Lord; then it was received of their hands and burnt upon the altar. Each had a different way it was waved or lifted up to the Most High before it was actually burnt and offered to the Lord.

“And thou shalt take the breast of the ram of Aaron’s consecration, and wave it for a wave offering before the Lord: and it shall be thy part.” The breast of the ram of consecration was waved and became the priest's part. The breast of the wave offering and “the shoulder of the heave offering, which is waved, and which is heaved up”, were sanctified, “And it shall be Aaron’s and his sons’ by a statute for ever from the children of Israel.”

That is the wave breast and the right shoulder of Numbers 18, the priests' part from the children of Israel for ever, “a covenant of salt for ever before the Lord unto thee and to thy seed with thee”, the children that come after them.

points: To hallow Aaron and his sons to minister in the priest's office: one young bullock and two rams without blemish, with unleavened bread, cakes tempered with oil, and wafers anointed with oil, brought in one basket to the door of the tabernacle of the congregation.

note.label: Exodus 29: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

points: And shalt wash them with water: cleanliness and spotlessness were very important to the Most High in everything dealing with the temple, and He is real specific and detailed about how clean and sanctified a man must be before he enters the holy place. This thread runs all through the first five books, Leviticus especially.

note.label: Exodus 29: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

points: The garments are put upon Aaron, the coat, the robe of the ephod, the ephod, and the breastplate, with the curious girdle; the mitre upon his head and the holy crown upon the mitre; the anointing oil poured upon his head; and his sons in coats, girdles, and bonnets. The priest's office shall be theirs for a perpetual statute: thou shalt consecrate Aaron and his sons.

Ecclesiasticus records the same consecration: Moses anointed him with holy oil, an everlasting covenant to Aaron and to his seed so long as the heavens should remain, to minister unto Him, execute the office of the priesthood, offer the sacrifices, and teach Jacob the testimonies and inform Israel in His laws. The priest's job was the offerings and teaching the nation the law, statutes, and commandments.

That is why leadership today is not walking around requiring Levite lineage of Aaron. note.label: Exodus 29: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

points: The bullock is killed before the Lord by the door of the tabernacle, its blood put upon the horns of the altar with the finger, the fat burnt upon the altar, and the flesh, skin, and dung burnt with fire without the camp: it is a sin offering. This is the introduction to the categories of offerings; there is the sin offering.

note.label: Exodus 29: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

points: The first ram is slain, its blood sprinkled round about upon the altar, and the whole ram burnt upon the altar: it is a burnt offering unto the Lord, a sweet savour, an offering made by fire. There is the second category, the burnt offering.

note.label: Exodus 29: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

points: The second ram is the ram of consecration: its blood is put upon the tip of the right ear of Aaron and of his sons, upon the thumb of their right hand and the great toe of their right foot, and sprinkled upon the altar round about; the blood and the anointing oil are sprinkled upon Aaron, his garments, his sons, and their garments, and he shall be hallowed.

These ordinances belonged to the Levitical priesthood, and the doctrines that would put men back under pieces of that office today do not even keep what they claim; they sound right because they use scriptures strongly and confidently, but they are in error. Be not tossed to and fro with every wind of doctrine, nor carried about with strange doctrines; do not ever fall away from the Messiah.

note.label: Exodus 29: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

points: The bread and the parts of the ram are put in the hands of Aaron and his sons and waved for a wave offering before the Lord, then burnt upon the altar; and the breast of the wave offering and the shoulder of the heave offering are sanctified for Aaron and his sons by a statute for ever. There go the wave offering and the heave offering, which you will read about throughout the first five books, Leviticus predominantly.

note.label: Exodus 29: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

points: The holy garments of Aaron pass to his sons after him, to be anointed and consecrated in them; the son that is priest in his stead shall put them on seven days when he cometh into the tabernacle to minister.

note.label: Exodus 29: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

points: Aaron and his sons eat the flesh of the ram and the bread at the door of the tabernacle, the things wherewith the atonement was made; a stranger shall not eat thereof, because they are holy. And whatever of the flesh or the bread remains unto the morning is burnt with fire and not eaten: no eating the leftovers of the offering, because it is holy.

note.label: Exodus 29: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

points: Seven days shalt thou consecrate them, offering every day a bullock for a sin offering for atonement, cleansing the altar and anointing it to sanctify it, that it be an altar most holy.

note.label: Exodus 29: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

points: Then the continual offering: two lambs of the first year day by day continually, one lamb in the morning and the other at even, with the tenth deal of flour mingled with beaten oil and the drink offering of wine; a continual burnt offering throughout your generations at the door of the tabernacle, where the Lord meets and speaks with Israel.

note.label: Exodus 29: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

points: The tabernacle shall be sanctified by His glory, and Aaron and his sons sanctified to minister in the priest's office; for the Most High to enter and deal with Israel, everything had to be sanctified. That was serious.
